definitions.gloss: Japanese-style; done in the Japanese manner
definitions.explanation: Designating something done in a distinctly Japanese way, in contrast to {西洋式|せいようしき} or {洋式|ようしき} (Western-style).

examples.japanese: {日本式|にほんしき}の{挨拶|あいさつ}。
{日本式|にほんしき}の{経営|けいえい}には{独特|どくとく}の{特徴|とくちょう}がある。
ローマ{字|じ}には{日本式|にほんしき}、ヘボン{式|しき}、{訓令|くんれい}{式|しき}などの{表記法|ひょうきほう}がある。
examples.english: For romaji there are several notations such as Nihon-shiki, Hepburn, and Kunrei-shiki.

notes:
Compound of {日本|にほん} (Japan) + the suffix {式|しき} (style, system). Often interchangeable with {和式|わしき}, though {和式|わしき} is more common for everyday physical items (especially {和式|わしき}トイレ) and {日本式|にほんしき} is more common for abstract systems (management, education, romanization).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- As a noun modifier: {日本式|にほんしき}の + noun
- As a predicate: {日本式|にほんしき}だ / です

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和式|わしき}: Japanese-style — more common for physical objects/facilities
- {日本|にほん}{風|ふう}: Japanese in feel — softer; a Japanese-like atmosphere or flavor
